description: Complete pacs.009 Financial Institution Credit Transfer demonstrating interbank transfer with optional elements. High-value USD transfer from Deutsche Bank (Germany) to JPMorgan Chase (US) via Bank of America intermediary using Fedwire clearing.
test_coverage: Complete group header with settlement information
Settlement method (CLRG) and clearing system (FED - Fedwire)
Complete payment identification (InstrId, EndToEndId, TxId, UETR for gpi tracking)
Payment type information (HIGH priority, G001 gpi service level)
Settlement time indication with debit date/time
Structured creditor information with postal address
Instructions for next agent (PHOB code with free text)
business_rules_expected_to_pass: PACS009-DT01: Settlement date not in past (2026-02-10)
PACS009-DT02: Settlement date not more than 90 days in future
PACS009-PT01: Creditor institution present with full details
PACS009-RF03: UETR in valid UUID format
PACS009-GH02: Transaction count consistency (1 CdtTrfTxInf, NbOfTxs=1)
business_rules_expected_to_fail: PACS009-RG01: High-value transfer controls (warning - amount exceeds 100,000)
notes: This message demonstrates a complete interbank transfer scenario: Deutsche Bank in Germany instructing JPMorgan Chase in the US to receive USD 250,000 via Fedwire clearing system, with Bank of America as intermediary. The HIGH priority and UETR tracking indicate this is a gpi-enabled transfer requiring same-day settlement. The instruction code PHOB indicates the beneficiary institution should be contacted by phone. This is semantically related to MT202 cover payments but uses ISO 20022 structure.
